stem.text: The volume of ammonia produced against time is measured in two experiments.
In experiment 1, 3 mol of $\text{H}_2\text{(g)}$ and 1 mol of $\text{N}_2\text{(g)}$ react together at $45\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ and a pressure of 200 atm.
A graph showing the volume of ammonia produced against time is plotted.
Experiment 2 is then performed. Experiment 2 differs from experiment 1 in **one** condition only.

stem.alt: Graph of volume of NH3 against time with two curves labelled experiment 1 and experiment 2; both start at the origin and level off, and the curves cross once.

stem.text: How does experiment 2 differ from experiment 1?

A.text: An iron catalyst is present in experiment 2.

B.text: 2 mol of helium gas is present in the reaction mixture in experiment 2.

C.text: A pressure of 250 atm is used in experiment 2.

D.text: A temperature of $600\,{}^{\circ}\text{C}$ is used in experiment 2.
